bill_text.text_with_changes:
A bill for an act relating to game and fish; prohibiting the use of sonar when fishing for muskellunge or northern pike in certain waters; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 97C.335.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 97C.335, is amended to read:

97C.335 [-USE OF-][+ RESTRICTIONS ON USING+] ARTIFICIAL LIGHTS [+AND SONAR +]TO TAKE FISH [-PROHIBITED-].

[+Subdivision 1.+]

[+Using lights prohibited.+]

(a) A person may not use artificial lights to lure or attract fish or to see fish in the water while spearing, except that while angling or spearing, a person may:
(1) affix a lighted artificial bait with hooks attached to the end of a fishing line; or
(2) use a lighted decoy for spearing.
(b) A battery that is used in lighted fishing lures must not contain mercury.
(c) The restrictions in paragraph (a) do not apply to bow fishing.

[+Subd. 2.+]

[+Using sonar.+]

[+(a) While fishing for muskellunge or northern pike in waters identified by the commissioner as waters where muskellunge populations are naturally reproducing and not primarily maintained through stocking, a person may not use, operate, or possess any of the following in an active or deployable state: +]

[+(1) live imaging sonar, forward-facing sonar, omnidirectional sonar, or drones; or +]

[+(2) equipment, software, or systems that use, integrate with, or enhance live imaging sonar, including but not limited to technologies employing artificial intelligence, predictive modeling, real-time data processing, or wireless communication between devices or components to locate, track, or target muskellunge or northern pike. +]

[+(b) Possession of any of the items described in paragraph (a) on waters identified by the commissioner as waters where muskellunge populations are naturally reproducing and not primarily maintained through stocking, shores of those waters, or islands in those waters is presumptive evidence that the person is in violation of this subdivision, unless: +]

[+(1) the equipment is powered off; +]

[+(2) the equipment has all power and transducer cables physically disconnected from the unit; +]

[+(3) the equipment has all disconnected power leads and transducer connections visibly secured in a manner that prevents immediate reconnection, including but not limited to being capped, taped, clamped, or otherwise enclosed; and +]

[+(4) the equipment, software, or systems cannot be made operational via wireless, remote, or software- or application-based activation without deliberate physical connection. +]
bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to game and fish; prohibiting the use of sonar when fishing for muskellunge or northern pike in certain waters; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 97C.335.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 97C.335, is amended to read:

97C.335 RESTRICTIONS ON USING ARTIFICIAL LIGHTS AND SONAR TO TAKE FISH .

Subdivision 1.

Using lights prohibited.

(a) A person may not use artificial lights to lure or attract fish or to see fish in the water while spearing, except that while angling or spearing, a person may:
(1) affix a lighted artificial bait with hooks attached to the end of a fishing line; or
(2) use a lighted decoy for spearing.
(b) A battery that is used in lighted fishing lures must not contain mercury.
(c) The restrictions in paragraph (a) do not apply to bow fishing.

Subd. 2.

Using sonar.

(a) While fishing for muskellunge or northern pike in waters identified by the commissioner as waters where muskellunge populations are naturally reproducing and not primarily maintained through stocking, a person may not use, operate, or possess any of the following in an active or deployable state:

(1) live imaging sonar, forward-facing sonar, omnidirectional sonar, or drones; or

(2) equipment, software, or systems that use, integrate with, or enhance live imaging sonar, including but not limited to technologies employing artificial intelligence, predictive modeling, real-time data processing, or wireless communication between devices or components to locate, track, or target muskellunge or northern pike.

(b) Possession of any of the items described in paragraph (a) on waters identified by the commissioner as waters where muskellunge populations are naturally reproducing and not primarily maintained through stocking, shores of those waters, or islands in those waters is presumptive evidence that the person is in violation of this subdivision, unless:

(1) the equipment is powered off;

(2) the equipment has all power and transducer cables physically disconnected from the unit;

(3) the equipment has all disconnected power leads and transducer connections visibly secured in a manner that prevents immediate reconnection, including but not limited to being capped, taped, clamped, or otherwise enclosed; and

(4) the equipment, software, or systems cannot be made operational via wireless, remote, or software- or application-based activation without deliberate physical connection.
